Any exception during this process (e.g., `ClassNotFoundException`, `InstantiationException`, `IllegalAccessException`, or `ClassCastException`) is caught by the generic `catch (Exception e)` block. The use of an unchecked exception suggests the programmer does not want to force callers to handle this error; rather, it should propagate upward as an unexpected runtime failure.
